name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,486

clue.text: Hot and cold ale is free to distribute round new place for students

indicators.note: distributing things spreads them about, so these letters are dealt out in a new order
the jumbled letters go round the outside of the next piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A student union bar handing out free beer, served hot and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot and cold' tempts as H and C, but only hot is abbreviated; cold is used whole. The anagram is wrapped round N, which sits just before the final CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall of residence is a university building where undergraduates live during term, so it is accommodation for students.

clue.text: Philosopher welcoming foot soldiers in part of station

indicators.note: a host welcoming a guest takes them inside, so the philosopher's name holds the next piece

blocks.note: the Greek philosopher, pupil of Socrates
F is the abbreviation for foot
the Royal Marines, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A thinker greeting infantrymen arriving at a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot soldiers' reads as one idea (infantry), but it splits: foot goes inside the philosopher and soldiers follow. The Royal Marines are Britain's naval infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: A platform is the raised area beside the track where passengers board trains, one section of a railway station.

clue.text: Host losing end of cracker in drink

indicators.note: losing an end means the final letter of the named word is dropped

blocks.note: to chair a meeting is to host or preside over it
the last letter of cracker, the one that is lost

explanation.surface: A party host who has lost the end of a Christmas cracker in a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAIR loses its last letter R, the end of cracker, leaving CHAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Chai is spiced tea, originally from India, a popular hot beverage.

clue.text: Sailor posted to Eastern Europe is a missing person

blocks.note: an able-bodied seaman, abbreviated AB
a letter posted has been sent
E for Eastern plus E for Europe

explanation.surface: A seaman sent abroad to Eastern Europe has been reported missing.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is someone who is not present where expected, such as a worker or voter who fails to turn up.

clue.text: Fish making slow progress

blocks.note: surface reading: a sluggish fish drifting through the water
setter's reading: moving lazily, without purpose, like an engine ticking over; 'Fish' hints at the ide and the ling, two fish whose names sit within the answer

explanation.surface: A lazy fish dawdling through the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer can be seen as ID + LING; the ide and the ling are both fish, which is the setter's nod in 'Fish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idling means passing time lazily or moving without hurry, which is barely getting anywhere at all.

clue.text: Reduction set to include staple source of cereal

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so the word for set encloses what follows
the source of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of cereal is used

blocks.note: to set something down is to put it
rice is a staple food for much of the world
the first letter of cereal

explanation.surface: A cut-price offer on a breakfast staple like cornflakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The staple and the cereal's first letter go in together as one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A price cut is a reduction in what something costs, the usual phrase for a discount.

clue.text: Country artist covering washed-out base of wood

indicators.note: covering something means lying round it, so the artist's letters surround the rest
the base of a down word is its bottom letter, so only the last of wood is used

blocks.note: a Royal Academician, abbreviated RA
wan means pale, colourless
the last letter of wood

explanation.surface: A painter putting a coat over faded timber.
explanation.walkthrough: R + WAN D + A: the artist's two letters wrap round WAN and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a landlocked nation in central-east Africa, so it is a country.

clue.text: Understanding hospital departments provided tablet and drink at end of procedure

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last of procedure is kept

blocks.note: two ear, nose and throat departments, each ENT
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet
a cordial is a sweet fruit drink
the last letter of procedure

explanation.surface: A patient handed a pill and a drink after an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'departments' gives ENT twice. E for an ecstasy pill is a standard crossword shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 agreement between Britain and France, so an entente is a friendly understanding between nations.

clue.text: God associated with a poor Indian city

blocks.note: the Arabic name for God
taken as written
poor quality is bad

explanation.surface: A deity linked with a poverty-stricken place in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Allahabad, now officially Prayagraj, is a large city in Uttar Pradesh where the Ganges and Yamuna meet.

clue.text: Fuss about North American tree

definitions.note: the American mountain ash is a rowan

blocks.note: a row is a noisy quarrel or fuss
A abbreviates about, as in approximately
N is the compass abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: A commotion about a tree from North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North American' reads as one phrase, but North gives its letter to the wordplay and American stays with the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, has species native to North America as well as Europe, so it qualifies as a tree there.

clue.text: Engineer let rain into bog

indicators.note: to engineer something is to construct or rig it, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A builder lets the rain pour into a marshy field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog' looks like a swamp, but it is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Bog is informal British for a lavatory, and a latrine is a basic toilet, as in a camp or barracks.

clue.text: Popular feeling expressed as anger

indicators.note: something expressed is put into speech, so the sound of the words counts, not their spelling

blocks.note: popular is IN, and a feeling is a SENSE

explanation.surface: Public mood comes out as fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them furious, so the verb means to enrage or anger.

clue.text: Sell fine piece of wood

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a log is a cut length of timber

explanation.surface: A timber merchant offering a good-quality plank for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: Flog is British slang for selling something, often cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: Flog is informal British for offloading goods to a buyer, as in flogging an old car.

clue.text: Cast get far developing theatrical skills

indicators.note: something developing is changing shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Actors making great progress in honing their performing abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as the actors in a play, which fits the theatre theme, but it is only letters to be reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagecraft is the art and technique of putting on plays, covering acting, direction and production know-how.

clue.text: Broadcast end of 'open sesame' as a group

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order
the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last of open is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of open
taken as written

explanation.surface: Transmitting the last part of Ali Baba's magic password.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open sesame' is the phrase that opens the robbers' cave in Ali Baba; only the N of open is used.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French borrowed into English meaning all together, as one body.

clue.text: Mistress finally leaving terrible control freak

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter, so only the final one of mistress is kept
something terrible is in a dreadful mess, so these letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the last letter of mistress
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lover finally walking out on a dreadful, domineering partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' looks like a deletion signal for the S, but it is fodder for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the sinister hypnotist in du Maurier's novel Trilby, gave his name to anyone who manipulates and dominates another person.

clue.text: Enormous heads of neoclassical icons found during attic conversion

indicators.note: heads are tops, so the first letter of each of the two words is taken
found during something means sitting inside it, so those letters go into the middle
a loft conversion remodels a space, so the letters of attic are rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, split around the inserted pair
the first letters of neoclassical and icons

explanation.surface: Huge statues in classical style turn up while someone converts a loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attic' plays on Attic Greek art to match the neoclassical icons, but here it is a loft whose letters are rearranged round NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means of colossal size or strength, from the Titans, the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Publican upended vessel over bird at end of bar

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning something upside down reads its letters from bottom to top
the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last of bar is used

blocks.note: a vat is a large tank or vessel
the erne is the sea eagle, a crossword regular
the last letter of bar

explanation.surface: A pub landlord tipping a barrel over a bird perched by the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' means the upturned vessel sits above the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverner is an old word for someone who keeps a tavern, so a landlord of an inn or pub.

clue.text: Changed ringtone element

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so these letters appear in a different order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has switched the sound their mobile phone makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is the chemical element with atomic number 7, the gas making up most of the air.

clue.text: Noteworthy setter's given gift-wrapped volume

indicators.note: a wrapped present encloses what it holds, so the word for gift goes round the volume

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself, so setter's is I'M
pressie is British slang for a present
V is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler has been handed a book wrapped as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: Pressie is British informal for a present; the volume goes in just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impressive commands attention or admiration, so it is worthy of notice.

clue.text: New leader of Labour party is insignificant

indicators.note: a new version is a remade one, so these letters are put in a fresh order
a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of Labour is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of Labour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political jibe: the fresh Labour leader counts for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Labour' was the Blair-era brand of Britain's Labour Party, which makes New look like part of the name rather than the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means trivial or meagre, of little worth or importance.

clue.text: Travel guide tucked into kosher paella

indicators.note: something tucked into food is buried inside it, so the answer lies within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A tour leader eating a kosher version of the Spanish rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' reads as eating, but it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famed as mountain guides and porters for climbing expeditions.

clue.text: Brilliant time to leave foundation

indicators.note: a letter that leaves the word is taken out of it

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
the foundation of something is its start

explanation.surface: An excellent moment to walk away from a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: START drops one T, its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Star as an adjective means outstanding or brilliant, as in a star pupil or star performance.

clue.text: European part of puzzle about old German literary work

indicators.note: about means around, so the puzzle part goes round the letters that follow

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a clue is one element of a crossword
O is the abbreviation for old
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A puzzle piece on an ancient German book.
explanation.walkthrough: The old and German letters sit in the middle of the puzzle part, after the European one.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short pastoral poem, such as Virgil's Eclogues, a recognised form of literature.

clue.text: Rabbi visiting Italy stirred oil into dish

indicators.note: stirring mixes the contents of a pan, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: Rav is the Hebrew title for a rabbi
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rabbi on holiday in Italy drizzling oil into his supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visiting' looks like a container signal, but RAV simply comes before I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli is an Italian pasta of small stuffed parcels, served as a dish.

clue.text: Struggle with appearance

blocks.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Someone battling with how they look.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is what can be seen, the sight or prospect something presents.

clue.text: Teething ring for child originally at an early stage of development

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the first letter of child is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of child

blocks.clueFragment: at an early stage of development
blocks.note: in Freudian theory the oral stage is the infant's first phase

explanation.surface: A baby's teether bought at the very start of growing up.
explanation.walkthrough: A coral was a traditional baby's teether, a polished stick of coral often set in a rattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished coral was once given to infants to chew while teething, so a coral was the name for such a toy.

clue.text: Dish given to cold English male cooked in stages

indicators.note: cooking changes the form of raw ingredients, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a pie is a baked dish
C is the tap abbreviation for cold
E is the abbreviation for English
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pie served to a chilly Englishman, prepared bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means done gradually, a part at a time rather than all at once.
